**Drives can't be locked out by a library update.** Each drive now records
the password-hashing settings it was made with, so a future update can't
change how its key is worked out from your password.

## Downloads

| Platform | File | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10/11 (x64) | `cloak-v0.3.3-windows-x64.zip` | [WinFsp](https://winfsp.dev) (`winget install WinFsp.WinFsp`) |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `cloak-v0.3.3-macos-arm64.dmg` | [macFUSE](https://macfuse.github.io) |

**Windows:** unzip and run `Cloak\Cloak.exe`. Keep the folder together: the
engine is in `Cloak\bin`, and your drive list and settings are kept in
`Cloak\cloak-data`.

**macOS:** open the disk image and drag **Cloak** onto **Applications**. The
app isn't notarized, so before opening it the first time, clear the download
quarantine: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Cloak.app` (or
right-click Cloak → Open, then Open again). macFUSE's kernel extension must be
allowed; on Apple Silicon that means its one-time Reduced Security setup.

## Fixed

- **Password settings are now fixed and saved with each drive.** Cloak turns
  your password into the drive's key with Argon2id. It used the library's
  default settings without recording them, so a future change to those
  defaults would have made every existing drive reject its correct password.
  The settings are now pinned in cloak, new drives record them in
  `meta.json`, and existing drives keep working unchanged: nothing to do.
- Settings read from a drive are checked, so a damaged `meta.json` gives a
  clear error instead of an unlock that runs out of memory.

## Compatibility

Drives and recovery backups made by this version open in v0.3.2, and the
other way round. Nothing about existing drives changes.

## Known limitations

- Auto-lock runs on sleep, not when the screen locks.
- The app isn't code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen may warn on first run
  (More info → Run anyway).
- The middle of every file stays plaintext on disk by design.
